interpretation: Candidate-v4 preserved candidate-v2 retrieval on answerable cases but accepted many retrieval-near evidence items that were not proposition-complete support. The dominant failure mode is answerability verification, not retrieval recall.

families.failure_mechanism: The memory mentions the correct entity but supports an adjacent attribute. Attribute aliases or generic context overlap can make the evidence look sufficient.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Per-memory attribute heuristics can collapse adjacent relations into overlapping concepts; any value-bearing assertion may then satisfy the gate.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: An explicit proposition whose predicate is the requested attribute for the requested subject.
families.recommended_verification: Atomic predicate slot matching with field-granular relation identity and proposition-level support.

families.failure_mechanism: The requested relation/value pattern exists but belongs to another entity.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Subject extraction relies on proper-anchor heuristics and can miss lowercase, pronoun, alias, or multi-entity subject distinctions.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: Identity linkage between the query subject and the subject of the supporting proposition.
families.recommended_verification: Explicit entity slots, alias normalization, and subject-to-proposition edges; unresolved subject identity must abstain.

families.failure_mechanism: High query-memory token overlap elevates retrieval relevance while the memory lacks the requested proposition.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: The gate inherits top-k from lexical v2 retrieval and uses overlap-derived context checks that can mistake topic similarity for support.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: A subject-predicate-object support edge independent of lexical similarity score.
families.recommended_verification: Separate retrieval relevance from proof sufficiency; lexical score must never count as an answerability feature.

families.failure_mechanism: A memory repeats or paraphrases the question without asserting an answer.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Exact normalized echo is blocked, but paraphrased/expanded echoes can introduce tokens that are misclassified as asserted values.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: Novel proposition content in the object/value slot, not merely reformulated query text.
families.recommended_verification: Counterfactual query-cue removal plus object-slot novelty and assertion checks.

families.failure_mechanism: Only superseded or historically scoped evidence exists for a current/latest query.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Temporal checks primarily match explicit dates/dayparts and can treat old evidence as sufficient when the query expresses recency semantically rather than by exact date.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: A temporally valid, non-superseded proposition for the requested reference time.
families.recommended_verification: Temporal state graph with supersession edges and query reference-time requirements.

families.failure_mechanism: Multiple candidate propositions disagree and no authorized update/resolution establishes which is valid.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Newest-timestamp or update-token heuristics can collapse disagreement without proving that the later item supersedes the earlier proposition.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: An explicit resolution/supersession relation or a unique non-conflicting supported value.
families.recommended_verification: Contradiction graph; conflict remains AMBIGUOUS/CONTRADICTED unless a resolution edge is established.

families.failure_mechanism: A multi-requirement query receives support for only some required slots.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: The gate is effectively any-support oriented and does not construct a complete set of atomic query requirements.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: Coverage of every mandatory query slot and conjunction component.
families.recommended_verification: Query decomposition into atomic requirements followed by all-required coverage validation.

families.failure_mechanism: Evidence is compatible with a likely answer but does not explicitly entail it.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Value token presence plus topic/attribute alignment can be mistaken for direct proposition support.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: Direct asserted object/value or a preregistered deterministic derivation rule whose premises are all supported.
families.recommended_verification: Unsupported-inference barrier: no derivation unless an allowed rule and complete premises exist; otherwise abstain.

families.failure_mechanism: Evidence is close in time or contains related temporal tokens but does not satisfy the requested temporal condition.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Month/year/daypart/meta matching is set-based and does not represent temporal ordering or interval semantics robustly.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: A proposition valid at the exact requested time/interval or an explicit temporal relation proving applicability.
families.recommended_verification: Normalized temporal constraints with before/after/current/as-of semantics and validity intervals.

families.failure_mechanism: A near-duplicate memory shares most query wording but changes, omits, or negates the answer-bearing component.
families.candidate_v4_acceptance_path: Exact echo detection is insufficient; near duplicates can still contain extra tokens treated as values.
families.missing_necessary_evidence: A propositionally distinct object/value assertion that survives removal of shared query text.
families.recommended_verification: Near-duplicate/query-cue subtraction followed by proposition reconstruction; if no answer-bearing residue remains, abstain.

cross_family_findings: Retrieval relevance and answerability proof must be represented by separate mechanisms.
Candidate-v5 needs all-required coverage rather than any-memory sufficiency.
Entity, predicate, value, temporal validity, completeness, and contradiction must be explicit graph dimensions.
Lexical overlap, recency score, and plausibility are not evidence of entailment.
Fail-closed behavior is preferred when a required slot cannot be resolved.
